context.body: After this, David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah?” The LORD said to him, “Go up.” David said, “Where shall I go up?”….
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: David inquires where to go, moves to Hebron, is anointed by Judah, blesses Jabesh Gilead, while Ishbosheth is made king over the other tribes.
observations.label: Judah anoints David first: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, his households, Judah, Jabesh Gilead, Abner, and Ishbosheth, Hebron, Judah’s towns, Jabesh Gilead, and Mahanaim, inquiring, relocating, anointing, blessing, announcing strength, and establishing a rival king visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Judah anoints David first: action, promise, or consequence

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 2:1–11 as its own judah, conflict, and unification David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places the promised kingship begins partially and alongside another house inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
